title: Neither victory nor defeat: SDF's dissolution marks new phase for Syria's Kurds, says Al Majalla's Ibrahim Hamidi
gist: An Al-Monitor podcast summary in which Al Majalla editor-in-chief Ibrahim Hamidi argues the Aug. 25, 2026 formal dissolution of the Syrian Democratic Forces, announced by commander Mazlum Kobane, is neither victory nor defeat for Syria's Kurds, and that Kobane's new role as advisor to President Ahmed al-Sharaa opens fresh opportunities even as many Kurds feel angered.

insights.claim: Syrian Democratic Forces commander-in-chief Mazlum Kobane announced on Aug. 25, 2026 that the force has been formally dissolved, angering many Kurds across the region.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Formal dissolution of the main Kurdish-led armed force reshapes Syria's security map and US-partner dynamics in the northeast.
insights.quote: the force has been formally dissolved
insights.locator: Many Kurds across the region feel angered

insights.claim: Al Majalla editor-in-chief Ibrahim Hamidi argues the SDF's dissolution is neither victory nor defeat and that the push for Kurdish rights is by no means over.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: A veteran analyst framing dissolution as a phase change rather than defeat signals the Kurdish question remains a live political variable in Syria.
insights.quote: the push for Kurdish rights is by no means over
insights.locator: Ibrahim Hamidi, a veteran Syrian journalist

insights.claim: Hamidi contends that Mazlum Kobane's new role as an advisor to Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa will present the Kurds with fresh opportunities.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Kobane's pivot into an advisory role in Damascus signals a channel for Kurdish influence within the new Syrian state to monitor.
insights.quote: will present the Kurds with fresh opportunities
insights.locator: Kobane's new role as an advisor to Syrian President
